merger_description:
As of May 2026, McDonald’s Australia Limited (**McDonald’s Australia**) owns 1,070 McDonald’s restaurants around Australia. It generally operates around 15% of these restaurants (**Corporate Restaurants**) and licenses the right to operate and occupy the remainder (**Franchised Restaurants**). Both the Corporate Restaurants and Franchised Restaurants supply McDonald’s branded fast-food products through dine in, takeaway, drive through and / or digital ordering channels.

Between 13 August 2007 and 13 February 2026, Kramford Pty Limited, Jayark Pty Limited as trustee for Jayark Trust, Sherlee Pty Limited as trustee for Sherlee Trust, Pipmay Pty Limited as trustee for Pipmay Trust, Frygirl Pty Ltd as trustee for Frygirl Trust, Gozoboy Pty Ltd as trustee for Gozoboy Trust (collectively, the **Franchisee**), Mark Andrew Halford (**Guarantor**) and McDonald’s Australia entered into franchise agreements or licences (**Franchise Agreements**) and occupation licences, leases or subleases (Occupation Agreements) in respect of the McDonald’s Dural, Kellyville, Rouse Hill, Rouse Hill Town Centre, Kellyville North, Norwest Marketown, Norwest II, Annangrove and Stanhope Gardens restaurants in NSW (**Target Restaurants**). These agreements granted the Franchisee the right to occupy and operate the Target Restaurants.

McDonald’s Australia, the Franchisee and the Guarantor propose to enter a Deed of Surrender, Release and Asset Purchase in respect of the Target Restaurants (**Buyback Agreement**). Pursuant to this Buyback Agreement the Franchisee will surrender the Franchise Agreements and Occupation Agreements to McDonald’s Australia and sell the property used in the Target Restaurants to McDonald’s Australia (the **Acquisition**).

The property of the Target Restaurants comprises:

1. any plant and equipment, fixtures and fittings used in connection with the Target Restaurants
2. all current and saleable trading stock, consumables, packaging and packaging materials, work-in-progress, raw materials and finished goods held, used or to be used in the Target Restaurants and
3. the benefit of the contracts that the Franchisee has entered in relation to the supply of goods or services to the Target Restaurants.

determination_table_content.details:
McDonald’s Australia Limited (McDonald’s Australia) applied for a
notification waiver in respect of its proposal to enter a Deed of
Surrender, Release and Asset Purchase with:
• Kramford Pty Limited, Jayark Pty Limited as trustee for
Jayark Trust, Sherlee Pty Limited as trustee for Sherlee
Trust, Pipmay Pty Limited as trustee for Pipmay Trust, Frygirl
Pty Ltd as trustee for Frygirl Trust, and Gozoboy Pty Ltd as
trustee for Gozoboy Trust (collectively, the Franchisee), and
• Mark Andrew Halford (the Guarantor)
in respect of 9 McDonald’s restaurants, namely the McDonald’s
Dural, Kellyville, Rouse Hill, Rouse Hill Town Centre, Kellyville North,
Norwest Marketown, Norwest II, Annangrove and Stanhope Gardens
restaurants (the Target Restaurants), as described in the transaction
documents provided as part of the application (the Acquisition).
The Acquisition will involve the Franchisee surrendering their
franchise agreements and occupation agreements to McDonald’s
Australia, and selling the property used in the Target Restaurants to
McDonald’s Australia.

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABV(1)(a) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.

The acquirer, McDonald’s Australia, owns 1,070 McDonald’s
restaurants around Australia. It generally operates around 15% of
these restaurants (Corporate Restaurants) and licenses the right to
operate and occupy the remainder (Franchised Restaurants).
The Target Restaurants are 9 McDonald’s restaurants, which are
currently licensed to the Franchisee and are located at:
• McDonald’s Dural: 823 Old Northern Rd, Dural 2158
• McDonald’s Kellyville: 658 Windsor Rd, Kellyville 2153
• McDonald’s Rouse Hill: 1 Resolution Place, Rouse Hill 2155
• McDonald’s Rouse Hill Town Centre: Rouse Hill Town Centre,
Rouse Hill 2155
• McDonald’s Kellyville North: 133 Samantha Riley Drive,
Kellyville 2155
• McDonald’s Norwest Marketown: Baulkham Hills 2153
• McDonald’s Norwest II: 2-6 Lexington Drive, Bella Vista 2153
• McDonald’s Annangrove: 7 Gymea Cct, Rouse Hill NSW 2155
• McDonald’s Stanhope Gardens: Shops 30 & 31, Stanhope
Village Centre, Stanhope Gardens 2768.
Both the Corporate Restaurants and Franchised Restaurants supply
McDonald’s branded fast-food products through dine in, takeaway,
drive through and / or digital ordering channels.

In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers that
the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening of
competition. In particular:
a. the Acquisition involves a transfer from the Franchisee to
the franchisor with no change in the number of McDonald’s
restaurants in the area
b. there are alternative providers of fast-food products in the
local areas surrounding the Target Restaurants
c. there is a low risk of foreclosure or other concerning vertical
effects post-acquisition.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s interim guidance on
notification waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
